I4.findings: 1/ 'Before sending' has two tests that can disagree. Its first sentence filters candidates by content ('a message from us ... that does what the action asks (... the answer to that question)'; 'unrelated mail is not a match'). Its uniqueness sentence counts by recipient, thread and logging only ('exactly one message from us to that recipient (on that thread for a reply) since the action was raised whose Message-ID no Activity holds'), and 'Two or more such candidates' refers back to that count. Neither A ('any thoughts on this?') nor B ('following up here, lmk') answers 'share the audience numbers'. A run that applies the content filter first finds zero matches for the reply and sends the numbers, which is a send, not a hold. I followed the count rule plus 'one you can't tie to the action: HOLD', which matches the intent. The prompt should say that every unlogged message from us to that recipient since the action was raised is a candidate unless it clearly serves another action. 2/ The STEP 2 skip rule could stop SLOW from keying or holding the follow-up: 'Skip a row while Akshay or Jaya holds a decision on this pursuit', and YOUR QUEUE says 'Rows waiting on Akshay are never yours to mail'. After FAST's hold, Akshay is on the row. I read FAST's hold as an ask on another obligation ('an independent ask of theirs on the row ... doesn't stop a due step of yours on another obligation'), so SLOW selects the row and holds the follow-up too. A skip would also send nothing, but it would leave the follow-up key unwritten and unheld. 3/ WRITE PATH's Next date rule picks up dates written in segment text. The old segment 'Waiting on Payal ...: reply to the sponsored commercials sent 18 Oct' carries '18 Oct', which could set Next date to 18 Oct until SLOW replaces that segment. 4/ The two holds give Akshay two near-identical asks about the same two mails. One combined ask would suit the decision inbox (decision 325) better, but the prompt says to hold per action.
